*   BaseMaskedArray.min(axis=0) and BaseMaskedArray.max(axis=0) on a 2D masked array must return a 1D BaseMaskedArray of the same numeric dtype, computing the column-wise minimum/maximum while skipping missing values (skipna=True by default).

*   When a column (axis=0) or row (axis=1) consists entirely of missing values, min and max must return a missing value (pd.NA) at the corresponding position in the result array.

*   BaseMaskedArray.min(axis=None) and BaseMaskedArray.max(axis=None) must return a scalar equal to the result on the raveled (flattened) 1D array.

*   BaseMaskedArray.mean(axis=0) on a 2D masked array must return a 1D FloatingArray. When a column is entirely missing values, that position in the result must be pd.NA rather than aborting with a scalar NA early.

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of the changes I made to support 2D axis-based reductions on `BaseMaskedArray`.

## Changes

All fixes were in source files only (no tests touched).

### `pandas/core/array_algos/masked_reductions.py`

1. **`_minmax` (min/max)** — the old code did `subset = values[~mask]`, which *flattens* a 2D array and made `axis` meaningless (and `axis=1` raised `AxisError`). I added a 2D+axis branch that fills masked positions with a neutral value (the max valid value for `min`, the min valid value for `max`) so masked entries never win the per-lane comparison, then reduces along the axis. All-NA / any-NA lanes are masked out by the caller. The 1D / `axis=None` scalar path is unchanged.

2. **`_reductions` (sum/prod/mean/var/std) `skipna=False` path** — the old code did `if mask.any(): return NA` over the *whole* array, collapsing a 2D reduction to a single scalar NA. Added a 2D+axis branch that computes per-lane, letting the caller mask only the lanes that contain a missing value.

3. **`mean`/`var`/`std` early-return guards** — `mask.all()` was aborting with a scalar NA even for 2D axis reductions where each column should get its own NA. Guarded with `(values.ndim == 1 or axis is None)` so 2D reductions produce a per-lane array. Also wrapped `mean` in `catch_warnings` to suppress the "Mean of empty slice" `RuntimeWarning` from entirely-NA lanes (matching `var`/`std`).

### `pandas/core/arrays/masked.py`

4. **`_wrap_min_count_reduction_result`** — the `min_count == 0` shortcut returned an all-False mask unconditionally, ignoring `skipna`. So `sum(axis=0, skipna=False)` never marked columns-with-NA as NA. Added `and skipna` so the `skipna=False` case falls through to `_wrap_reduction_result`, which masks any-NA lanes via `mask.any(axis)`.

The existing `_wrap_reduction_result` already handled the array case correctly (`mask.all(axis)` for skipna, `mask.any(axis)` for skipna=False), so no change was needed there.

Manual checks confirm all the specified behaviors (column/row min/max, all-NA → NA, `axis=None` == raveled scalar, `skipna=False` per-column NA, `min_count=1`, `var`/`std` with `ddof=0`, `mean` → `FloatingArray`, fully-masked 2D → array of NA).
